"API certified" isn't a marketing word. It's the difference between documented and theoretical.
Any bentonite can claim it meets a spec on paper. Certified bentonite has to prove it, batch by batch, with a certificate of analysis you can actually check.

Uncertified material is the opposite: consistency you're told to assume, not consistency you can verify. And on a bentonite, inconsistency shows up in two places.

First, filtration control. A batch that runs off-spec on filtrate loss won't seal the bore wall properly, you get a weak filter cake, fluid loss into the formation, and a wall that wants to slough before the concrete goes in.

Second, sand content. Uncertified bentonite typically carries more inert material, clay that isn't doing any clay's job, plus grit that is doing damage. That sand doesn't build viscosity or hold cuttings. It just wears out your pumps, your shaker screens, and your seals, batch after batch.

Certification doesn't make the clay smarter. It makes the consistency provable, so what passed on the COA is what's actually going into your bore.
Are you checking the COA on every batch, or just on the first one?

Built for the ground that wants to cave in before the concrete goes in.
Construct Gel is Blick's construction-grade bentonite for bored piles, diaphragm walls, and foundation drilling in soft, saturated, or unstable ground, tested to ISO 13500 Clause 9 / API Spec 13A Section 9 on every batch, not just the first one off the line.

It holds the bore open on hydrostatic pressure and builds a filter cake fast enough to seal the wall before it sloughs. Across our last three COA-tested batches, filtrate volume came in at 14.6 ml every time (limit is 15 ml max), the kind of batch-to-batch consistency that keeps your fluid program predictable instead of a guessing game.

Dosed 14, 100 kg/m³ depending on ground conditions (30, 45 kg/m³ typical for well-conditioned water), and stocked in AU and NZ.
Specifying bentonite for an upcoming piling or diaphragm wall job? Talk to our technical team before you finalise the fluid program.
